authority_provenance.standing_authority: #458 SS3.1 migrationStrategy + SS6 X-16 ruling + SS7 child-issue charter (adopted M1 decomposition, R2/R3-reviewed): tier-1 migrates the reachable context-face test consumers onto the six submit_*/Request<T> spellings with the attach_observer three-test exemption (SS3.1 blockers 5) and the five zero-symbol include deletions, wires B-02, defers Batch to the F2 B-01 re-freeze batch (blockers 6), keeps the identity_of fallback dormant (blockers 2); tier-2 = X-16 explicit policy isolation pending F3 (SS6).
authority_provenance.option_a_role: #459 comment 6055510469 packages that standing authority as the execution sequence Option A. Every action executed in #468/#469/#471 maps to an SS3.1/SS6 clause; Option B contradicted SS6 clause 2 and SS3.1 blockers 6, and Option C required unadopted faces, so Option A was the only packaging consistent with standing authority. Its selection was authority-neutral execution sequencing, not a new human ruling.
authority_provenance.corrected_misattribution: The #459 ruling comment's authorization-source paragraph cited the Execution Lead directive's conditional sentence together with the #458 orchestration comment (6055084231, which disclaims ruling status) as the authorization source. That sentence is prioritized execution advice from the repo owner, not a recorded authority ruling, and is no longer cited as authority.
authority_provenance.ratification_status: No GitHub artifact records the human authority owner explicitly ratifying the Option A record itself. The M-R claims in this overlay do not depend on that ratification: they stand on #458 SS3.1/SS6. An explicit confirmation comment on #459 by the authority owner would upgrade the chain to direct ratification (requested; optional, non-blocking).
